extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and IPOPHL examiners/practitioners interacting with the Philippine patent office
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive regulatory rules governing amendments, withdrawals, revival, grant, fees, assignments, corrections, petitions, and appeals in patent prosecution before the IPOPHL (Philippine Intellectual Property Office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 918: Amendment and Revision Required
rubrics_metrics.description: The description, claims, and drawings must be amended and revised, when required, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, or unnecessary prolixity, and to secure correspondence between the description, claims, and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 919: Amendment of the Disclosure (No New Matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: No deletion or addition shall broaden the disclosure of an application to include new matter after the filing date. All amendments made after filing must conform to at least one of the parts (description, claims, drawings) as of the filing date. Matter not found in the original disclosure cannot be added even if supported by a supplemental oath and must be the subject of a separate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 920: Amendment of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be amended by canceling particular claims, by presenting new claims, or by amending the language of particular claims (such amended claims are treated as new claims). Applicant must point out how new or amended claims avoid any reference or ground of refusal of record pertinent to them and indicate which part of the original disclosure constitutes the basis of the amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To facilitate examination, indicate in the response which part of the original disclosure is the basis of the amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 921: Manner of Making Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not make erasures, additions, insertions, or alterations directly on papers and records. Amendments are made by filing a request for amendment together with a clean copy of the amended text. Exact words to be stricken or inserted and the precise points must be specified. The basis of proposed amendments in the original application shall be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clean copy of amended parts; specify exact words and precise insertion/deletion points; indicate basis in original filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 922(a): Entry of Amendments by Office (red-ink convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are entered by the Office by drawing a red line through cancelled words and making proposed substitutions or insertions in red ink; small insertions are written at the designated place and large insertions are indicated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 922(b): Consideration of Amendments (timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily all amendments presented while the application is open to amendments are entered and considered; untimely amendatory papers may be refused entry or may be considered in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness affects entry/consideration; improper amendments may be later cancelled or corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 923: Amendments to the Drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: No change in the drawing may be made except by permission of the Office. A request for change must be accompanied by payment of the required fee and a sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes. The request should be separate from other papers. Drawings may not be pulled out except for signature. Substitute drawings will not ordinarily be admitted unless required by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File a separate paper, include a permanent-ink sketch, pay required fee; substitute drawings are exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 924: Amendment of Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendatory clause is to be amended, it should be wholly rewritten and the original insertion cancelled so that no interlineations or deletions appear in the clause as finally presented. Matters cancelled by amendment can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the cancelled matter as a new insertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid interlineations; wholly rewrite amendatory clauses; reinstatement requires new insertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 925: Substitute Description
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number or nature of amendments makes consideration or paper arrangement difficult, the Examiner may require the entire description, claims, or part thereof to be rewritten. A substitute description will ordinarily not be accepted unless required by the Examiner and may be required within two months from grant prior to publication of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may order substitute description where necessary for clarity/printing; generally only upon Examiner's requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 926: Numbering of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbering of claims is mandatory and numbers appearing at filing must be preserved throughout prosecution. When claims are deleted, remaining claims must not be renumbered. Added or replaced claims must be numbered consecutively beginning with the number following the highest previously presented claim. Upon allowance the Examiner may renumber claims consecutively in the order they appear or as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not renumber remaining claims after deletions; added claims must follow numerically; Examiner may renumber at allowance if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 927: Petition from Refusal to Admit Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: From refusal of the Examiner to admit an amendment, in whole or in part, a petition for admittance of such amendment may be filed before the Director under the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 928: Withdrawal for Failure to Respond within Time Limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is provided a maximum period of two months from the mailing date of the official action to file a response. Failure to prosecute within required time causes the application to be deemed withdrawn; a Notice of Withdrawn Application will be mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) two-month response period; (b) see extensions policy in following paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 928(b): Extension of Time for Reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for reply may be extended only for good and sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. Requests for extension must be filed no later than the day the response is due. Examiner may grant only one request for extension for a maximum of two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one extension per action allowed; must show good cause and file on or before due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 928(c): What Constitutes Prosecution to Save from Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution to save the application must include complete and proper action as the condition of the case may require. Any amendment or response not responsive to the last official action will not operate to save the application from being deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be responsive to the last official action to avoid withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 928(d): Opportunity to Supply Omissions for Bona Fide Attempts
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant's action is a bona fide attempt to advance the case and is substantially complete but inadvertently omitted some matter or compliance, opportunity may be given to explain and supply the omission before withdrawal is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may allow cure of inadvertent omissions in substantially complete bona fide responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 928(e): Unsigned/Improperly Signed Papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt ratification or filing of a correctly signed copy may be accepted in case of an unsigned or improperly signed paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 929: Revival of Application (with cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application deemed withdrawn for failure to prosecute may be revived within three months from the mailing date of the notice of withdrawal if shown to the Director that failure was due to fraud, accident, mistake, or excusable negligence. A petition to revive must be accompanied by a showing of justifiable reason, a complete proposed response, and full payment of required fee. Failure to provide these causes denial. No revival if previously revived with cost. Submission of response without filing petition will not automatically revive. Application not revived is deemed forfeited and a Notice of Forfeiture will be mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must demonstrate specific grounds (fraud/accident/mistake/excusable negligence), include proposed response and full fee; previous revival with cost precludes another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 929.1: Revival Without Cost (Office fault)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application deemed withdrawn due to loss of applicant's response or Examiner's action not received (evidenced by post office return card) or other unforeseen circumstances considered fault of the Office may be revived without cost if petition filed within three months from mailing date of notice. For loss of applicant's response, petition must include the copy bearing original Office stamp. If petition to revive without cost is denied, applicant may seek revival with cost (except where denial based on being filed out of time) within one month from notice of denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival without cost is limited to Office-fault situations and has strict documentary proof and time limits; denial based on late filing prevents revival with cost if out-of-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 930: Voluntary Withdrawal of Application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be voluntarily withdrawn by filing a verified declaration of withdrawal identifying the application and signed by applicant or assignee of record. A voluntarily withdrawn application shall not be revived and will be deemed forfeited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 930.1: Publication of Declaration of Withdrawal and Opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Once verified declaration of withdrawal is filed and application identified, the declaration and withdrawal shall be published in the IPOPHL E-Gazette within 15 days for purposes of opposition. If the declaration was filed prior to first publication, the declaration and application shall not be published and shall be deemed withdrawn by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication enables third parties to file Opposition within 15 days of publication (with fees and sworn statement substantiated by evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 930.1: Opposition Requirements to Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition to withdrawal must be a written sworn statement with personal information, circumstances of affiant, reasons why affiant will be prejudiced, substantiated by evidence or proof, and accompanied by payment of fees. Office will dismiss submissions failing to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict compliance required; Office will notify petitioners of oppositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 930.2: Director Decision on Opposition to Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall decide whether Opposition should be granted and the voluntary withdrawal shall be held in abeyance until Opposition resolved. If Director grants Opposition and refuses withdrawal, applicant may appeal to Director General; no motion for reconsideration allowed. If Director denies Opposition and grants withdrawal, application deemed withdrawn as of date decision issued and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 931: Reconstitution of Application File Wrappers
rubrics_metrics.description: Office maintains physical and/or digital records. A file wrapper or document declared lost may be reconstituted only if application remains active; withdrawn or forfeited applications cannot be reconstituted. Petition for reconstitution with fees must be filed stating facts/circumstances and prosecution history, and must attach a carbon original or duplicate copy containing Office acknowledgement receipt; mere photocopies not acceptable. Office will deny petitions if records are found or application had been withdrawn/forfeited prior to petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide authenticated copies with Office acknowledgement; active application only; fees required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1000: Grant of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application meets requirements of the IP Code and these Regulations, the Office shall grant the patent, provided all fees are paid on time. If fees for grant and printing are not paid in due time, the application shall be deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of required fees on time is a condition precedent to grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1001: Contents of Patent (form and legal effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent shall be issued in the name of the Republic of the Philippines under the Office seal and signed by the Director of Patents, and registered together with the description, claims, and drawings. A digitally signed Letters Patent or Certificate of Registration has same legal effect as traditional signature; electronic certificates have same effect as physical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1002: Publication upon Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant of the patent, together with other information, shall be published in the IPOPHL E-Gazette within six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1003: Inspection of Patent File
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party may inspect the complete description, claims, and drawings of the patent on file with the Office. Marginal notes and exchanges between applicant and Office shall not be included. Inspection by other international IP offices pursuant to agreements shall be governed by provisions of those agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1004: Term of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Term shall be twenty (20) years from the filing date of the application. Patent ceases to be in force if prescribed annual fees are not paid within the prescribed time or if cancelled per IP Code and Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1100: Annual Fees (due timing and payment rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: First annual fee is due on expiration of four years from date application is published, and on each subsequent anniversary. Payment for annual fee and claims in excess of five must be made in full and may be made within three months before due date. Obligation to pay terminates if application withdrawn, forfeited, refused, or cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims-in-excess fees payable; annual payments may be made up to 3 months before due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1100 (Divisional Applications): Annual Fees for Divisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: For divisional applications, first and succeeding annual fees payable on expiration of four years from publication date of parent application and every year thereafter. If divisional filed more than 4 years from publication of parent, annuity payments for divisional commence the year following the last annuity payment date of parent; divisional pays only remaining claims covering subject matter of parent in subsequent payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special timing rules when divisional filed later; pay corresponding annuity according to anniversary of parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1100.1: Annual Fees for Divisional Applications (further detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: For divisionals filed more than four years from parent publication, annuity payment of divisional commences following year from last annuity payment date of parent and on each subsequent anniversary. Divisional will pay annuity fee according to current anniversary of parent until expiration of term of parent. For Direct Route and PCT National Phase applications, annuity due upon expiration of four years from date parent application was published and on each subsequent anniversary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1101: Date Application is Published
rubrics_metrics.description: Application is published on the date the IPOPHL E-Gazette containing the application is released for circulation (example provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use E-Gazette release date to compute annuity due dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1102: Non-payment of Annual Fees; Grace Period and Consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If annual fee and excess claims fees not paid within prescribed time, notice of non-payment published in E-Gazette and mailed to patent owner/applicant/agent. Within a six-month grace period from publication of the notice, annual fee plus surcharge for delayed payment and publication fee must be paid in full. Failure leads to notice that application deemed forfeited or patent considered lapsed as of day following expiration of original period; recorded in appropriate register. If only excess-claims fee unpaid, notice to pay deficit issued and unpaid excess claims are disregarded for further prosecution or cancelled from patent protection. An application deemed forfeited or patent lapsed for non-payment cannot be revived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six-month grace period applies after publication of non-payment notice; unpaid excess claims may be cancelled; non-revivable forfeiture/lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1200: Form of Assignment (requirements for recordal)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be acceptable for recording, an assignment must be in writing; if not in English/Filipino, accompanied by English translation; acknowledged before a notary or authorized officer and certified under seal; accompanied by appointment of resident agent if assignee not resident; must identify the patent/application by number/date/name/title or by date/executant/name/title if executed before filing; accompanied by required recordal and publication fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct identification of patent/application and required notarization/translations and fees; appointment of resident agent if assignee foreign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1201: Form of Other Instruments Affecting Title (including licenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other instruments affecting title, including licenses, must conform with requirements of Rule 1200 to be acceptable for recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1202: Assignment and Other Instruments to be Submitted in Duplicate
rubrics_metrics.description: Original document together with a signed duplicate shall be submitted. If original not available, an authenticated copy in duplicate may be submitted. After recording, Office retains the signed duplicate or one authenticated copy and returns the original or other authenticated copy with notation of recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit original + signed duplicate (or authenticated duplicates); Office keeps duplicate and returns original with recording notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1203: Date of Recording is Date of Filing; Effect on Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of recording of assignment or instrument is date of its receipt by Office in proper form and accompanied by full payment of required recording and publication fees. Such instruments shall be void against subsequent purchaser/mortgager without notice unless recorded within three months from date thereof or prior to subsequent purchase/mortgage. Notice of recording published in E-Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record promptly to protect against subsequent purchasers; full fees and proper form required for recording date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1204: Letters Patent May be Issued to Assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of assignment of a pending application, letters patent may be issued to the assignee provided assignment has been recorded before actual issue of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1205: Assignee May Act in Office Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any action in any proceeding in the Office which may or must be taken by a patentee or applicant may be taken by the assignee, provided the assignment has been recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1206: Surrender of Patent (voluntary cancellation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner of patent, with written sworn and verified consent of all persons having recorded grants/licenses/other rights, may surrender patent or any claim(s) for cancellation and voluntary surrender. Petition must be in writing, sworn, verified and authenticated if executed abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All recorded rights-holders must consent in writing and verification; petition formalities required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1206.1: Publication and Opposition to Petition for Cancellation/Surrender
rubrics_metrics.description: Once petition for cancellation and voluntary surrender filed and patent identified, petition shall be published in E-Gazette within 15 days. Within 15 days from publication any person may present a written Opposition with payment of fees; Opposition must be sworn and substantiated by evidence. Office will notify petitioners. Submissions not complying will be dismissed. If no Opposition or dismissed, and Director satisfied, petition granted and patent deemed surrendered as of publication date; patent ceases to have effect but no infringement actions or compensation for prior use by government shall lie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition process and strict compliance requirements; publication triggers 15-day opposition window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1206.2: Director Decision on Opposition to Surrender
rubrics_metrics.description: Director decides whether Opposition should be granted and surrender held in abeyance until resolved. If Director grants Opposition and refuses surrender, applicant may appeal to Director General; no motion for reconsideration allowed. If Director denies Opposition and grants surrender, patent deemed surrendered and published as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1207: Correction of Mistakes of the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon written petition in duplicate of patentee or assignee and upon tender of copy of patent issued to patentee, Director may correct without fee any mistake in a patent incurred through fault of the Office when clearly disclosed by records, to make patent conform to records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office-fault mistakes may be corrected without fee; petition and copy of patent required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1208: Correction of Mistakes in the Application (clerical/formal)
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of any interested person and payment of prescribed fee, Director authorized to correct any mistake in the patent of a formal and clerical nature not incurred through the fault of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal/clerical errors (not Office fault) can be corrected upon petition and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1209: Changes in Patent (scope and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may request Office to make changes in the patent to: (a) limit extent of protection through deletion of claim(s); (b) correct obvious mistakes or clerical errors; (c) correct mistakes or errors other than clerical made in good faith. Where change would broaden protection, no request may be made after two years from grant and change shall not affect rights of any third party who relied on published patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations on broadening changes (two-year window); ensure third-party rights not affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1209.1: Corrections Limited to Administrative Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: All corrections in Rule 1209 shall be limited to corrections which are administrative in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1209.2: No Post-Grant Claim Amendments Requiring Re-Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes or amendments that involve claim amendments which will require re-examination of the application shall not be accepted since prosecution on the merits was concluded when the patent was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant claim-amendments requiring re-examination are barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1210: Form and Publication of Amendments or Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment or correction of a patent shall be accomplished by a certificate of such amendment or correction, authenticated by Office seal and signed by Director, which certificate shall be attached to the patent. Notice of such amendment/correction shall be published in E-Gazette and copies of patent furnished by Office shall include copy of the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1211: Corrected or Revised Copies of Certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: If Office grants corrections or revisions, owner may request corrected/revised certificate upon filing request, payment of fees, and surrender of original owner's copy. Office shall release corrected/revised certificate marked as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1211.1: Duplicate Copies of Certificates (lost owner's copy)
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner's copy of Certificate is lost, owner may request duplicate upon filing request, payment of fees, and accompanying notarized Affidavit of Loss. Office shall release duplicate marked as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit of Loss required for duplicate certificate issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1212: Assignment and Transmission of Rights (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents or applications and related inventions shall be protected as property under Civil Code. Inventions and any right, title, or interest may be assigned or transmitted by inheritance or bequest or be subject of a license contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1213: Assignment of Inventions (scope and territorial limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment may be of entire right, title, or interest or an undivided share (joint ownership). An assignment may be limited to a specified territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1214: Rights of Joint Owners
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more persons jointly own a patent, each joint owner is entitled to personally make, use, sell, or import the invention for his own profit; however, neither joint owner may grant licenses or assign rights without consent of other owners or without proportionally dividing proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1300: Nature of Examiners' Function (quasi-judicial and discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining whether an application should be allowed or refused is a quasi-judicial function involving judicial discretion. The Director cannot lawfully exercise direct control over Examiners regarding such determinations but only general supervision via review of recommendations and adverse decisions by petition or appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1301: Petition to Director on Matters Not Subject to Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions may be filed to the Director from any repeated action or requirement of the Examiner not subject to appeal and in other appropriate circumstances. Petitions must comply with time and manner prescribed; briefs or memoranda should accompany or be embodied in the petition. Examiner may be directed to furnish a written Examiner's Brief. Filing of petition does not stay the maximum four-month period for replying to Examiner's action nor stay other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include supporting briefs; Examiner may be ordered to respond; petition filing generally does not stay deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1302: Appeals to the Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant may appeal to the Director upon final refusal of the Examiner to grant a patent. Appeal may also be taken from any adverse Examiner action within original jurisdiction. A second adverse Examiner decision on same grounds may be considered final for purposes of appeal. Appeals must comply with time and manner prescribed in Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1302.1: Director May Inhibit from Deciding Appeal or Petition
rubrics_metrics.description: After preliminary review of facts, the Director may inhibit from rendering a decision if conflict of interest exists; Director issues a Resolution stating reasons and directs Assistant Director to render decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1303: Effect of Final Examiner Decision Not Appealed (res judicata)
rubrics_metrics.description: A final decision of an Examiner not appealed within permitted time (or appealed but not prosecuted) is final and has the effect of res judicata for subsequent action on same subject matter. If application is considered withdrawn for failure to respond on the merits, the order declaring application forfeited for failure to file petition for revival likewise has res judicata effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1304: Time and Manner of Petition or Appeal (filing requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition or appeal must be filed in duplicate within a non-extendible period of two months from the mailing date of the action subject to petition or appeal, with full payment of required fee. The petition/appeal must specify facts, points to be reviewed, grounds for petition/appeal, and be signed and verified by petitioner/appellant or attorney of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-month non-extendible filing period; duplicate filing; specify facts and grounds; verification required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1305: Appellant's Brief Required
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of an appeal, appellant shall file an Appellant's Brief within a non-extendible thirty (30) days from filing of notice of appeal. The brief shall contain authorities and arguments relied upon. Appeal dismissed for failure to file brief within time allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thirty-day non-extendible deadline for brief; include authorities/arguments; failure to file leads to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1306: Examiner's Answer (Examiner's Brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall submit to the Director an Examiner's brief containing a written statement in answer to petition or appellant's brief within thirty (30) days from issuance of an order directing submission. Copy shall be served on petitioner/appellant by the Examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's answer timeframe 30 days after Director's order; service to appellant required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1307: Appellant's Reply
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal, appellant may file a reply brief directed only to new points raised in the Examiner's answer within a non-extendible thirty (30) days from receipt of Examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply limited to new points raised by Examiner; 30-day non-extendible deadline.
